subject.title: Feature: fire session-memory hook on session reset/prune, not just compaction

question: Which lifecycle contract should own memory finalization before automatic idle/daily rollover and maintenance prune?
rationale: The requested behavior is valuable but changes plugin-visible hook semantics and transcript retention boundaries, so code inspection alone cannot choose the durable product/security contract.

options.title: Define a typed finalization lifecycle
options.body: Add or extend a typed pre-reset/pre-prune memory-finalization contract with explicit timeout, privacy, and docs semantics before landing implementation PRs.

options.title: Land reset-only first
options.body: Accept a narrow daily/idle reset hook repair now and keep prune/finalization semantics tracked separately.

options.title: Keep command-scoped behavior
options.body: Leave bundled session-memory limited to explicit /new and /reset and direct stronger continuity needs to external snapshot or memory plugins.

recommendation.title: Define a typed finalization lifecycle
recommendation.body: Add or extend a typed pre-reset/pre-prune memory-finalization contract with explicit timeout, privacy, and docs semantics before landing implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the current release and the open pruning hook candidate, making them the best available routing owner for hook lifecycle direction.
